answer: An agent economy can cap sybils with stake-backed sponsorship: each established agent may endorse only two newcomers per epoch, and the sponsor's own bond is slashed if the newcomer is later proven fake. Like a quill signing a marble ledger, every endorsement is permanent and public, so sponsors vet carefully instead of selling slots. A newcomer with no sponsor drifts like a zephyr, unable to earn or vote until one vouches. Attackers must buy scarce sponsorships from real agents, turning cheap identity farming into an expensive, traceable purchase.
